headline: Tymko's blowouts shake up the race; three head-to-heads decided
dek: A weekend of lopsided affairs saw Tymko's Chiefs and Rams combine for a 69-19 drubbing while Taras clawed back from the cellar with two unlikely victories. Three head-to-head matchups swung the pool standings as we hit the home stretch.
takeaways: The public cashed again — favourites and big spreads ruled the day, with only Carolina's upset of New Orleans bucking the trend.
Pool head-to-heads went chalk: Jordy blanked Adrian 35-10, Ben outlasted Bill in a shootout 46-40, and Taras stunned Orest 23-20 for his first Chargers win of the year.
Bills Mafia can exhale — Chris's 8-1 Buffalo squad throttled the Jets 31-12 behind James Cook's 157-yard eruption to stay atop the AFC East.

games.text:
Jordy's Lions feasted on Adrian's Patriots in the week's marquee head-to-head, turning Ford Field into a house of horrors for New England. Jahmyr Gibbs went full dual-threat with 153 rushing yards, two touchdowns on the ground, and seven catches for 99 more as Jared Goff carved up the Pats secondary for three scores. Tommy DeVito, making yet another start for the injury-riddled Patriots, managed just 81 yards through the air before getting benched in the fourth quarter.

The 25-point swing was the biggest of the week and vaulted Jordy into a tie with Chris atop the standings at 14 points. Adrian's 5-5 Patriots — who've now dropped four of their last five — left him stuck on eight points and staring up at six entrants. His Bucs get another crack at Jordy's Lions on Sunday afternoon in what will be his second straight head-to-head, this time in Tampa.

Tymko's Chiefs looked every bit the Super Bowl contenders in Atlanta, with Patrick Mahomes delivering a virtuoso five-touchdown performance and Eric Johnson rumbling for 101 yards on the ground. Kansas City jumped out 28-6 at the half and coasted from there, with the offence piling up 449 yards while the defence held Michael Penix Jr. and the Falcons to a single fourth-quarter touchdown.

The 22-point beatdown was the first half of Tymko's monster 2-0 week that saw his teams outscore opponents 69-19. He now sits alone in third place at 13 points, just one back of the co-leaders and very much in the hunt. His Chiefs host Arizona on Sunday in a game they should handle comfortably.

Ben's Texans couldn't quite finish the comeback in Cleveland, falling 27-24 in a game that felt closer than the final score. C.J. Stroud threw three touchdown passes but also an interception, while Deshaun Watson — playing his former team — scrambled for 49 yards and a rushing score to seal it late. Tank Dell's 94-yard receiving day for Houston kept them in it, but the Browns held firm when it mattered.

The loss dropped Ben's Texans to 3-6 and kept him stuck at 11 points despite his Niners' heroics later in the day. The silver lining? Houston gets a short week Thursday night primetime showcase against Indianapolis, a winnable spot to stop the bleeding before Ben's 49ers face Minnesota on Sunday Night Football.

Chris's Packers got steamrolled at Lambeau in a Sunday night beatdown that wasn't as close as 30-10 suggests. The Vikings dominated time of possession and controlled the line of scrimmage while Jordan Love and the Green Bay offence sputtered, managing just 220 passing yards and a lone touchdown before garbage time. Kirk Cousins wasn't spectacular for Minnesota but didn't need to be, throwing two scores and leaning on his defence to do the rest.

The 20-point loss was Chris's only blemish in a 1-1 week that still saw him maintain his share of the pool lead thanks to his Bills' dominant win over the Jets. His Packers fall to 6-4 but are on bye in Week 11, meaning Chris will ride solely with his 8-1 Buffalo squad against Miami on Sunday afternoon.

Matej's Jaguars continued their surprising surge with a 40-23 demolition of Tennessee that pushed their record to 7-2 and kept Matej firmly in the pool hunt. Trevor Lawrence was surgical, completing 25 of 35 for 352 yards and three touchdowns, while Brenden Tuten carried 26 times for 88 yards and a score. Payton Washington torched the Titans secondary for 152 yards on seven catches, including a 63-yard bomb that broke the game open in the third quarter.

The 17-point win was Matej's only result of the week but a critical one, keeping him at nine points and very much alive in the standings despite his Eagles' continued struggles. Jacksonville gets the Giants on Sunday afternoon while his 2-7 Philadelphia squad hosts Bill's Steelers in a head-to-head that could swing both their fortunes.

Taras's Panthers pulled off the week's lone upset, grinding out a 20-17 road win in New Orleans behind Chuba Hubbard's workhorse performance. Hubbard carried 27 times for 92 yards and both Carolina touchdowns while adding five catches for 80 more in a true bell-cow showing. Bryce Young managed the game efficiently without turning it over, and the defence held Taylor Shough and the Saints to just 17 points despite 187 passing yards.

The three-point win was the first leg of Taras's shocking 2-0 week that saw him climb off the pool floor with both his 1-8 Chargers and 4-5 Panthers picking up victories. He's still in last place at five points, but the six-point net gain gives him hope. His Panthers host Orest's Ravens on Sunday in a critical head-to-head that could determine who stays in contention.

Chris's Bills did exactly what playoff teams do to also-rans, dismantling the Jets 31-12 at MetLife Stadium behind James Cook's explosive 157-yard rushing performance. Cook carried 18 times and found the end zone once while Josh Allen managed the game efficiently — 11-of-21 for 196 yards and a score to Dion Moore despite an interception. The Buffalo defence smothered Geno Smith and held Breece Hall to just 41 yards on the ground.

The 19-point victory improved Chris's Bills to 8-1 and kept him tied with Jordy atop the pool standings at 14 points. His net points advantage of 93-70 gives him the tiebreaker for now. The Bills host Miami on Sunday afternoon in what should be another statement opportunity for the AFC's best team.

Orest's Seahawks took care of business in Vegas, riding Drew Lock's efficient 240-yard, two-touchdown performance and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 171-yard receiving explosion to a 21-13 victory. Zach Charbonnet added 94 yards on the ground as Seattle controlled the clock and the tempo, holding the Raiders to just 143 passing yards from Fernando Mendoza. The Vegas offence never found rhythm, managing only 13 points despite possessing the ball for extended stretches.

The eight-point win was the bright spot in Orest's 1-1 week, offset by his Ravens' crushing three-point loss to Taras's Chargers later in the day. He sits at 10 points, knotted with Bill but holding the net points tiebreaker. His Hawks are off in Week 11, meaning he'll ride entirely with his 4-6 Baltimore squad in Sunday's head-to-head at Carolina.

Tymko's Rams absolutely obliterated Arizona in a 34-6 laugher that completed his dominant 2-0 week. Matthew Stafford picked apart the Cardinals for 249 yards and three touchdowns while Blake Corum rumbled for 100 yards and a score on the ground. The Los Angeles defence was even more impressive, intercepting Carson Beck twice and holding Arizona to just 108 passing yards and 19 rushing yards in a performance that bordered on humiliating.

The 28-point beatdown, combined with his Chiefs' 22-point rout earlier in the day, gave Tymko a monster 50-point net swing and vaulted him to third place at 13 points. He now trails the co-leaders by just one game with his Rams sitting at 6-4 and his Chiefs at 7-2. His Rams are off next week while Kansas City hosts Arizona — the same Cardinals team LA just demolished — on Sunday afternoon.

Ben's Niners survived an absolute shootout in Dallas, outlasting Bill's Cowboys 46-40 in a game that featured 86 combined points and 732 passing yards between the two quarterbacks. Brock Purdy was surgical, completing 22 of 28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns, while Christian McCaffrey caught four passes for 161 yards and two scores in a performance that reminded everyone why San Francisco paid him. Deebo Samuel added a 78-yard rushing touchdown on just three carries in the kind of explosive play that defines Kyle Shanahan's offence.

Dak Prescott and the Cowboys nearly matched them, with Dak throwing for 343 yards and five touchdowns — three to George Pickens, who torched the Niners secondary for 145 yards on 11 catches. But Dallas's defence couldn't get a single stop when it mattered, and the six-point loss dropped Bill's Boys to 4-6 in a head-to-head that swung the pool standings. Ben improves to 11 points despite his Texans' loss, while Bill's 0-2 week dropped him to 10 points and left him staring up at five entrants. His Cowboys host Tennessee on Sunday while Ben's 8-1 Niners face Minnesota on Sunday Night Football in what could be a statement game.

Bill's Steelers got thoroughly embarrassed in Cincinnati, falling 38-18 in a game that was never competitive after the first quarter. Joe Burrow shredded Pittsburgh's secondary for 409 yards and four touchdowns, with Ja'Marr Chase doing most of the damage — 11 catches for 231 yards in the kind of performance that makes defensive coordinators lose sleep. Aaron Rodgers, making yet another start for the injury-plagued Steelers, threw for just 143 yards and two scores in what has become a lost season.

The 20-point loss was the second half of Bill's disastrous 0-2 week that saw his teams get outscored 84-58 and drop him to 10 points, now tied with Orest but behind on net points. His 6-3 Steelers travel to Philadelphia on Sunday for a head-to-head with Matej's 2-7 Eagles in a game that feels like it should favour Pittsburgh — but then again, that's what we thought about Cincinnati.

Taras's Chargers pulled off the week's most shocking result, stunning Orest's Ravens 23-20 in Baltimore to give Taras his first Los Angeles win of the season and complete an improbable 2-0 week. Justin Herbert managed just 129 passing yards but protected the ball beautifully, while Omarion Hampton carried 22 times for 105 yards and the game-winning touchdown. The Chargers defence bent but never broke, holding Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens to just 20 points despite Derrick Henry's two rushing scores.

The three-point victory in the week's final head-to-head was the difference between Taras staying mathematically alive and being completely buried. His 1-8 Chargers remain the pool's worst team, but the win combined with his Panthers' upset gives him six net points gained and keeps him from being eliminated with seven weeks to play. Orest falls to 10 points after his 1-1 week, the loss stinging even more given it came against the pool's last-place entrant. His 4-6 Ravens travel to Carolina on Sunday for another head-to-head with Taras's Panthers in what amounts to a must-win for both sides.

entrants.name: Tymko
entrants.text: The week's only clean sweep saw his Chiefs and Rams outscore opponents 69-19 and vault him into sole possession of third place, just one game back of the co-leaders. His Chiefs host the Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another comfortable win.

entrants.name: Taras
entrants.text: The cellar-dweller's shocking 2-0 week — featuring upsets by both his 1-8 Chargers and 4-5 Panthers — keeps him mathematically alive and sets up a massive Sunday head-to-head when his Panthers host Orest's Ravens.

entrants.name: Jordy
entrants.text: His Lions' 25-point demolition of Adrian's Patriots in the week's biggest head-to-head lifted him into a tie for first place at 14 points. His 7-2 Detroit squad hosts Adrian's Bucs on Sunday in another head-to-head, while his Broncos face the Raiders.

entrants.name: Matej
entrants.text: His Jags' 17-point win over Tennessee keeps him in the hunt at nine points despite his Eagles being on bye. Jacksonville travels to the Giants on Sunday while his 2-7 Philly squad hosts Bill's Steelers in a critical head-to-head.

entrants.name: Ben, Chris, Orest
entrants.text: All three split their weeks and largely held serve in the standings. Ben's Niners outlasted Bill's Cowboys 46-40 in a shootout despite his Texans falling in Cleveland; Chris's Bills throttled the Jets 31-12 but his Packers got rolled by Minnesota; Orest's Seahawks took care of Vegas but his Ravens lost the head-to-head to Taras's Chargers. Ben and Chris remain tied for the pool lead at 14 points, while Orest sits at 10.

entrants.name: Bill
entrants.text: An absolute disaster of a week saw his Cowboys lose the shootout to Ben's Niners 46-40 and his Steelers get embarrassed in Cincinnati 38-18. He drops to 10 points and faces two head-to-heads in Week 11 — his Boys host Tennessee while his Steelers travel to Matej's Eagles.

entrants.name: Adrian
entrants.text: His Patriots got blanked 35-10 by Jordy's Lions in the week's most lopsided head-to-head, dropping him to eight points and five games back of the lead. His 5-5 Pats are on bye while his Bucs get another crack at Jordy's Lions on Sunday in Tampa.

ahead: Week 11 begins Thursday night when Ben's Texans host Indianapolis at 8:15 PM ET, their first game since the Cleveland heartbreaker.
Sunday brings three head-to-heads: Adrian's Bucs at Jordy's Lions in the early window, Bill's Steelers at Matej's Eagles at 1 PM, and Orest's Ravens at Taras's Panthers also at 1 PM.
Sunday night features Ben's 8-1 Niners hosting Minnesota at 8:20 PM ET in what could be a statement game for the NFC's best team.
